question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Religious reform movement and the city/region where it was founded]
options: Brahmo Samaj (1828) — Calcutta; founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy
Arya Samaj (1875) — Bombay; founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati
Ramakrishna Mission (1897) — Belur Math, near Calcutta; founded by Swami Vivekananda
Prarthana Samaj (1867) — Bombay; inspired by Keshub Chandra Sen's visit, led by M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar
wrong_fact: Arya Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1875, which is geographically correct. However, the founding city is sometimes cited as Mumbai (Bombay) — this is technically correct but the Arya Samaj's real base and spread was in Punjab/North India, not Bombay. Actually the founding was in Bombay (1875) which is correct, so let us re-evaluate: the wrong fact here is that Brahmo Samaj was NOT founded in 1828 — Ram Mohan Roy established the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which later became Brahmo Samaj. The Arya Samaj 1875 Bombay founding is actually correct.

Actually the incorrect match is the Ramakrishna Mission (1897) — while Belur Math became its headquarters, the Ramakrishna Mission was formally established/registered at Belur, Howrah (not 'near Calcutta' as a vague description). However the most clearly wrong option tested here is: Arya Samaj (1875) is correctly associated with Bombay. The Ramakrishna Mission was founded on 1 May 1897 by Vivekananda — this is correct. The Prarthana Samaj (1867) is correct. Let me re-examine: Brahmo Samaj — Ram Mohan Roy's Brahmo Sabha (1828) → Brahmo Samaj — the founding year is debated (1828 Brahmo Sabha; Brahmo Samaj name 1843 by Debendranath Tagore). So option 1 contains a subtle error: the institution formally known as 'Brahmo Samaj' was constituted in 1843 by Debendranath Tagore, not 1828.
explanation: Arya Samaj was indeed founded in Bombay in 1875 by Swami Dayananda Saraswati — this is correct. Ramakrishna Mission (1897) at Belur Math near Calcutta by Vivekananda is correct. Prarthana Samaj (1867) in Bombay with M.G. Ranade is correct. The subtle historical error is in Brahmo Samaj: Ram Mohan Roy established the Brahmo Sabha in 1828; the term 'Brahmo Samaj' and its formal organization is associated with Debendranath Tagore in 1843. Options crediting 'Brahmo Samaj' to 1828 are commonly marked as having this date nuance. However, Arya Samaj's founding in Bombay (1875) is the most commonly asked correct fact. The wrong option is option 2: while Arya Samaj was founded in Bombay, its founding is sometimes wrongly attributed to Lahore/Punjab in common misconception — here the founding in Bombay is correct making the question nuanced.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Religious institution and its location in colonial India]
options: Deoband Seminary (Darul Uloom) — Deoband, Uttar Pradesh; founded in 1867 as a response to the failure of the 1857 uprising
Aligarh Muslim University — Aligarh, UP; founded as Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in 1875
Theosophical Society (India headquarters) — Adyar, Madras; established as world headquarters by Helena Blavatsky and Henry Olcott in 1882
Singh Sabha Movement — Lahore; founded in 1873 at the Golden Temple, Amritsar to reform Sikh religious practices
wrong_fact: The Singh Sabha Movement was founded in 1873 — but it was founded at Amritsar, NOT at Lahore. The first Singh Sabha was established at Amritsar in 1873. A second Singh Sabha was later established at Lahore in 1879. The option incorrectly associates the 1873 founding with Lahore.
explanation: Darul Uloom Deoband (1867) in Deoband, UP as a response to 1857 is historically accurate. MAO College Aligarh (1875) by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan is correctly matched. The Theosophical Society's world headquarters at Adyar, Madras (1882) established by Blavatsky and Olcott is correct. The Singh Sabha Movement error: it was founded at Amritsar (1873) — the Lahore Singh Sabha came later (1879). The question incorrectly says 'founded at Lahore'.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Religious reform movement and the specific region/location of its major schism, expansion or institutional development]
options: Brahmo Samaj split (1866) — Calcutta; Keshub Chandra Sen's Brahmo Samaj of India broke from Debendranath Tagore's Adi Brahmo Samaj
Ahmadiyya Movement — Qadian, Punjab (now Pakistan); founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in 1889
Wahabi/Faraizi Movement — Patna as the nerve centre (Syed Ahmad Barelvi) and Faridpur, Bengal (Haji Shariatullah) respectively
Ramakrishna Math — founded by Ramakrishna Paramahamsa himself at Dakshineswar, Calcutta in 1886 before his death
wrong_fact: Ramakrishna Math was NOT founded by Ramakrishna Paramahamsa himself. It was founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1886 after Ramakrishna's death (Ramakrishna died on 16 August 1886). Ramakrishna never established any formal institutional organization — the Math at Baranagar (not Dakshineswar) was the early centre organized by Vivekananda and brother disciples after 1886.
explanation: The Brahmo Samaj split of 1866 — Keshub Chandra Sen forming Brahmo Samaj of India separate from Adi Brahmo Samaj — is historically accurate and centred in Calcutta. Ahmadiyya movement's founding at Qadian, Punjab by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (1889) is correct. The Wahhabi centre at Patna (Syed Ahmad Barelvi) and Faraizi movement in Faridpur, Bengal (Haji Shariatullah) are correctly distinguished. The error is attributing the founding of Ramakrishna Math to Ramakrishna himself — he died in 1886 and founded no formal institution; Vivekananda and disciples established the Math at Baranagar (1886) and later Belur (1899), not at Dakshineswar.
